title: Base change of a chosen pro-etale cover and its internal finite presentations
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes, $R$ a commutative ring object in $\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathrm{Ab})$ with its sheaf tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor, sk-def-sfb-ring-object], and $M$ an internal $R$-module [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. For every scheme morphism $g$, write $g^*$ for inverse image of abelian sheaves with its strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-finite-upper-star, def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal], and $T_g=\operatorname{mapMod}(g^*)$ for transport of internal modules [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. Let $\{u_i\colon U_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ be a pro-étale covering [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. Suppose that for each $i$ there are specified integers $m_i,n_i\ge0$, a module morphism $d_i\colon(u_i^*R)^{m_i}\to(u_i^*R)^{n_i}$, and an isomorphism $T_{u_i}M\cong\operatorname{coker}(d_i)$ [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Put $V_i=X\times_Y U_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $v_i\colon V_i\to X$ and $h_i\colon V_i\to U_i$.

Then $\{v_i\}_{i\in I}$ is a pro-étale covering of $X$. The inverse-image composition comparison for $f\circ v_i=u_i\circ h_i$ gives a ring-object isomorphism $\beta_i\colon v_i^*f^*R\xrightarrow{\sim}h_i^*u_i^*R$ and a module isomorphism
$$T_{v_i}T_fM\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\beta_i}(T_{h_i}T_{u_i}M).$$
Here restriction of scalars is [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For every $k\ge0$ there is a canonical finite-free identification
$$\operatorname{Res}_{\beta_i}T_{h_i}((u_i^*R)^k)\cong(v_i^*f^*R)^k.$$
If $d'_i$ is $\operatorname{Res}_{\beta_i}T_{h_i}(d_i)$ conjugated by these identifications, the displayed module isomorphism and the specified presentation induce
$$T_{v_i}T_fM\cong\operatorname{coker}\bigl(d'_i\colon(v_i^*f^*R)^{m_i}\to(v_i^*f^*R)^{n_i}\bigr).$$
In particular $T_fM$ is locally finitely presented [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented], witnessed on this specified base-changed cover with these same ranks. No flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $R$ or $f$.

proof.text: Use the existing abelian sheaf categories, their monoidal preadditive structure, and preservation of finite colimits by tensor. The source-library module-object category is abelian with finite colimits computed by the forgetful functor. Inverse image preserves finite colimits as a left adjoint. These instances apply to every morphism and all rings, including the zero ring.

source.place: Final two sentences: ambient hypotheses for right exactness and finite free modules; Stacks 0038 (categories.tex, lemma-adjoint-exact), 010N (homology.tex, lemma-exact-functor)

proof.text: Apply the existing Mathlib base-change operation on ZeroHypercovers for the pro-etale precoverage, whose definition already supplies its base-change stability instance. This is exactly the original index family, with objects pullback f (u_i) and maps pullback.fst f (u_i). Its mem₀ proves the first conclusion. Retain the unit-route weakly-etale stability module that supplies the mathematical stability statement.

source.place: Sentence 'Its base change'; Stacks 022D (topologies.tex, lemma-fpqc), part (3)

proof.text: The specified inverse-image compositor is the conjugate of the pushforward compositor. The monoidal adjunctions, their composite, and the monoidal pushforward compositor therefore give its monoidality by isMonoidal_conjugateEquiv_symm (equivalently the unit/counit mate calculation in the original plan). Equality congruence is monoidal by equality elimination. Compose these transformations to prove monoidality of the actual upperStarCompIso. Its component at R is a monoid isomorphism; monObjObj_comp identifies the composite structures with the actual iterated ring structures.

source.place: Pullbacks compose and the cover restriction comparison; explicit unit/counit expression of the mate, using the monoidal pushforward compositor and the specified monoidal adjunctions

proof.text: For the component at M, write both transported actions as tensorator followed by the image of the action. Naturality at the original action and the monoidality tensor equation give linearity after restriction along beta. Mod.isoMk supplies the inverse, proving the module comparison with exactly the component of the specified natural isomorphism as underlying morphism.

source.place: The restriction of pullback is pullback of the restriction: linearity of the specified composition comparison

proof.text: Let T be H.mapMod followed by restriction along beta. Its composite with the forgetful functor is H.mapMod followed by the other forgetful functor, definitionally. Finite colimits of module objects are computed in the ambient abelian categories and the forgetful functors reflect them, so T preserves finite colimits. It is additive by rightExactFunctor_le_additiveFunctor. This uses the already implemented preservesFiniteColimits_mapMod and reflection lemmas, without constructing another module adjunction.

source.place: Sentence "The pullback is right exact"; Stacks 0038 (categories.tex, lemma-adjoint-exact), part (1)

proof.text: The inverse ring map beta inverse identifies T of the regular module with the regular module for the source ring: linearity follows by the monoid-hom multiplication equation and cancellation of beta followed by beta inverse. For each k use T.mapBiproduct followed by biproduct.mapIso of this regular-module isomorphism on each summand. The mapBiproduct_hom, biproduct.map_π, and lift_π equations show that each coordinate is precisely H(pi_j) followed by beta inverse. Finite biproduct preservation includes k=0 automatically.

source.place: Sentence "it carries free modules of finite rank to free modules of the same rank"; explicit restriction across the ring isomorphism

proof.text: Set d prime = a_m inverse followed by T(d) followed by a_n. Compose PreservesCokernel.iso T d with cokernel.mapIso for the commuting square with vertical maps a_m,a_n, then precede it by T of p and the module comparison. This is the required presentationIso. To verify its normalization, expand functoriality on cokernel.pi d followed by p inverse; cancel the module comparison and p inverse followed by p, apply PreservesCokernel.pi_iso_hom and cokernel.pi_map, and cancel a_n inverse followed by a_n. Thus the cokernel arrow agrees exactly with the displayed arrow, rather than only up to an unspecified automorphism.

source.place: Final sentence: the actual transported differential, cokernel arrow and induced presentation

proof.text: Use the base-changed cover of step 2 and the presentations of step 7. For the existential predicate with its u-small cover index, apply ZeroHypercover.restrictIndexOfSmall to this cover, using Mathlib's existing Small instance for propQCPrecoverage. The module and map on each restricted index are definitionally those of the original family, so the presentation witnesses IsFinitelyPresented with ranks n_i,m_i in the order required by that definition. The canonical witnesses themselves still retain every original index. No nonzero rank, nonempty cover, flatness or Noetherian assumption is introduced.

source.place: Final sentence: local finite presentation on the specified base-changed cover
